players.note: Kyle Hamilton was rock solid in Week 3, tallying four solos, four assists, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended. The DB8 through three weeks of action, Hamilton is one of only four players linked to the top-12 in draft rooms who has been a DB1 so far. Tap Hamilton as a top-five option for a tasty Week 4 matchup against Cam Ward and the Tennessee Titans.

Dillon Thieneman impressed in Week 3, racking up four solos, two assists, one interception, and one pass defended. The rookie safety is settling in as a DB2 option; he has 15 solos on the season, and the best has yet to come. Count Thieneman as an upside top-25 play for Week 4, thanks to a plus matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Jordan Battle showed up in Week 3, racking up three solos, one assist, one interception, and one pass defended. Battle offers solid DB2 value, but is unlikely to crack the DB1 code unless he can show some more consistency and upside in the solo department. Tap him as a top-20 option for Week 4.

Jeremy Chinn was excellent in Week 3, racking up seven solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. The DB5 through three weeks of action, Chinn is locked in the top-10 conversation and should be treated as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Talanoa Hufanga went off in Week 3, exploding for two solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, two interceptions, three passes defended, and one touchdown. The AFC Defensive Player of the Week has been locked in as a DB1 option through three weeks of action, with the massive spike week pushing him up to DB1 overall in fantasy points. Continue to treat Hufanga as a top-1
0 option for Week 4.

Xavier Watts showed up in Week 3, tallying two solos, three assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Watts has produced like more of a borderline DB2 than the elite DB2 many expected him to be, but maintains his top-15 weekly upside. Tap him as a top-25 option for Monday Night Football against the New Orleans Saints.

Brandon Jones exploded for 10 solos, two assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended for the Denver Broncos in Week 3. Jones saw more snaps in the box due to facing off against the Los Angeles Rams and their 12 and 13 personnel heavy offense, and responded with what will likely be his season high in solo tackles. Jones is a strong DB3 option for Week 4 and beyond and should be rostered in all competitive leagues. Treat him as such for what should be another busy afternoon against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 4.

Joshua Metellus showed up in Week 3, tallying four solos, five assists, 0.5 sacks, and one pass defended. Metellus has just 11 solos on the season, but has managed four solos in two straight. He remains a DB3 option, but is teetering on the DB4 periphery. Tap him as a top-36 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Xavier McKinney showed up in Week 3, racking up four solos, one assist, one interception, and one pass defended. Xavier has slipped to the DB3 realm due to his slow start, but his Week 3 production swings his fantasy arrow back in the right direction. Treat McKinney as a top-36 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the banged-up Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Kamari Lassiter showed up in Week 3, tallying six solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss. Lassiter is locked in as an upside-based DB3 option who doubles as a CB1 in CB leagues. He is a proven IDP asset, playing opposite Derek Stingley, and should see plenty of work this weekend against the Dallas Cowboys. Tap Lassiter as a top-30 option, thanks to the plus matchup.

Chuck Clark was excellent in Week 3, racking up three solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Clark offers solid DB3 value as a starter for the Lions, a role he should have at least until the Lions return from bye in Week 7. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Alontae Taylor stepped up in Week 3, racking up four solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Taylor has recorded four or more solos in two straight games and remains locked in as a CB1/DB3 option. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

CJGJ showed up in Week 3 for the Buffalo Bills, notching three solos, two assists, one interception, and two passes defended.  Gardner-Johnson remains a top-25 option, but has lost some of his IDP upside due to playing more of his snaps deep in the Bills' defensive scheme. He is still more than worthy of a DB2 or even a DB3 play, but we can no longer expect him to push for DB1 numbers over the course of a full season sans at least a handful of interceptions. Tap CJGJ as a top-25 option for a suddenly tasty Week 4 matchup against the New England Patriots.

Reed Blankenship showed up in Week 3, tallying five solos, four assists, one interception, and two passes defended.  Blankenship has been a solid DB3 option to open the season, but flashed some of his DB2 upside against Indianapolis. For now, continue to treat him as a DB3 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Andre Cisco was at it again in Week 3, tallying five solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. He has recorded at least four solos in every game this season and made for a strong DB3 option with what turned out to be DB2 upside. However, Minkah Fitzpatrick was able to log a limited practice session on a Wednesday, suggesting that he may be able to suit up for Week 4, which in turn would send Cisco back to the bench. It was a good run for Cisco, but he is likely to see minimal (if any) snaps once Minkah is healthy. Prepare contingency plans for Week 4.

Christian Izien stepped up in Week 3, reeling off nine solos, two assists, three tackles for loss, and one pass defended on 97 percent of the snaps. Izien played just 36 percent of the snaps in Week 2, but played nearly every snap in Week 3 with Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph still sidelined. Izien should have at least one more start for IDP managers who find themselves in a bind and makes for an intriguing low-end DB3.

Hezekiah Masses was at it again in Week 3, reeling off four solos, two assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Masses now has a highly impressive three interceptions in two weeks filling in for the injured Darien Porter (foot), and may not be ready to give the starting role back. Masses has recorded four solos in two straight games, proving to be a worthy CB2/DB4 candidate if he continues to get starts. He is more of a deep league and speculative add, but Masses has shown enough to be worth a roster spot in leagues with deep benches.

Ronnie Hickman was excellent in Week 3, reeling off three solos, five assists, one interception, and one pass defended.  Hickman has recorded a sack or a pick in two straight games, ensuring that Emmanuel McNeil-Warren stays bolted to the bench outside of three safety looks. Hickman should have bought himself plenty of runway with his strong play to start the season. Add that to the Browns' surprsing early season success, and EMW may have to wait until late in the season, or even 2027, before he ascends to the starting lineup. This means Hickman projects as a safe DB3 option with no threat of losing his job during the byes. Tap him as a top-36 option for Thursday Night Football.

Dru Phillips was excellent in Week 3, racking up eight solos and three assists. Dru is a proven CB2 commodity who can double as a DB3 option in 20+ team leagues. However, for those of us in 12 team DB leagues, Phillips is not yet much of a fantasy option outside of a spot start in a heavy bye. He does play in the slot, which is why he offers some value outside of 32 team leagues, but will need to show more consistency to be viewed as a reliable DB3 option. Look elsewhere for Week 4.

Mansoor Delane showed up in Week 3, registering seven solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Mansoor played an every snap role for the Chiefs and should offer strong CB2 value for IDP managers. He has not yet entered the DB3 conversation but could join the discussion during the byes,

Amik Robertson stepped up in Week 3, tallying four solos, two assists, one forced fumble, and four passes defended. Amik has recorded four or more solos in two straight games, putting him in the CB2/DB4 mix. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. If you need a DB3, however, look elsewhere, at least until the byes.

Marcus Harris stayed hot in Week 3, reeling off five solos, two assists, and two tackles for loss. Harris has been shining in his slot role, recording at least four solos and two assists in every game this season. His consistency has locked him into the DB3 conversation during the byes and has propelled him to elite CB1 territory. At this point, Harris is one of the few corners who deserve to be plugged into lineups, even outside of the byes. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Taron Johnson was a busy man on Sunday, racking up seven solos, one assist, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended against the New Orleans Saints. Johnson is playing in the slot for Las Vegas, so he could settle in as a DB3 option eventually. For now, he is more of a CB league play, where he can be counted as a borderline CB1 option. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Renardo Green solidified himself as a CB2 option with his second strong game in three weeks, recording seven solos, six assists, and one pass defended. Green registered just three combined solos in his prior two games but had a pick in Week 1, which is what helps keep him on the CB2 radar as opposed to just being someone to add to watch lists. Roster him in CB leagues, but keep him on benches unless you need a CB3.

C.J. Henderson showed out in Week 3, reeling off eight solos and three passes defended. Henderson is being handed an expanded role with A.J. Terrell landing on I.R.and responded with an impact performance while leading the cornerback group in snaps. Henderson becomes an immediate CB2 option and could work his way into the CB1/DB1 co
nversation during the byes.

Genesis Smith made a name for himself on Sunday, breaking out with two solos, three assists, two interceptions, and two passes defended on 63 percent of the snaps. Smith has seen his snap share grow each week and has likely earned the full confidence of the coaching staff. Derwin James, of course, has the more valuable role of the starting safety duo, but Smith has proven he can be an IDP option despite playing the bulk of his snaps deep.

Quinyon Mitchell was at it again in Week 3, tallying six solos, one assist, two tackles for loss, and two passes defended. Mitchell is a top-12 CB option due to his upside and production and could be a solid DB3 option during the byes. For now, treat him as a CB1/DB4 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

Calen Bullock was at it again in Week 3, racking up five solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss. Bullock has recorded five solos in both of his games this season, keeping him locked in as a DB2 option. Treat him as a top-25 play for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.
